content:
Bloomberg reports that Apple may unveil the next-generation Mac mini in the coming days, ahead of the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra launch event scheduled for next month. Details are as follows.

It is highly likely to be the final product launch under CEO Tim Cook's tenure.

According to Mark Gurman's report, Apple is "preparing to release the first update to the Mac mini desktop computer in nearly two years," driven by a surge in demand in recent months, partly due to users wanting to run AI applications and models locally.

Excerpt from the report:

Gurman added that Apple has internally tested versions equipped with the M5 and M6 processors, while the upcoming new iMac is reportedly set to use the M6 chip.

Tonight's report comes just weeks after Apple reaffirmed that it would begin production of the Mac mini at its Houston facility later this year, when Tim Cook was accompanying Trump administration officials on a tour of the plant.

The same location houses Apple's new Advanced Manufacturing Center, which has already been used to produce and ship the company's AI servers. Apple stated earlier this month that it has invested hundreds of millions of dollars in the facility in less than nine months.

It remains unclear whether the new Mac mini to be announced in the coming days is the model Apple plans to produce in Houston later this year, although the likelihood appears considerably higher.

Gurman also reiterated in his report various developments in Apple's Mac product line over the coming months:

More Mac models will follow shortly after, though on a later timeline. These include an iMac in new colours and a redesigned entry-level MacBook Pro. Both will feature the next-generation M6 chip. The most significant Mac release in the lineup will be Apple's first computer with a touchscreen. The company will add this feature to new 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pro models, which will also feature a redesigned chassis and OLED displays.

Looking further ahead, Gurman reiterated earlier reports that Apple plans to introduce all-new MacBook Air and MacBook Neo models next year, as well as a second-generation touchscreen MacBook Pro powered by the M7 chip.
